slot_note: Wave 4 Forecasting. Architecture 2 after architecture 1 (the SBA 7(a) relief-era CECL allowance priced on guarantor groups) was spent at stage 4 (judge SEND_BACK, rule 3 AT_RISK, a task133-like shell). The seed FC19's lending world is left behind: redrawn in Urban & Regional Science, a county 911 center's late-shift answer-time forecast.
niche: a consolidated county 911 center's FY2028 staffing request: in which months of fiscal 2028 the Friday and Saturday late shift (22:00 to 02:00) will fall short of answering 90 per cent of 911 calls within 15 seconds with the four funded call-takers, once the state grant paying a fifth ends, so a seasonal fifth call-taker is funded for those months, when the regional 911 board's forecast adds a township whose 911 service moves over from the neighbouring county, 911 callers hang up when they wait, and the late shift's callers give up far sooner than the week's
answer: July 2027, August 2027 and June 2028 fall below 90 per cent with four call-takers (88, 89 and 89 per cent; September 2027 and May 2028 at 91, the other months 93 to 95): a seasonal fifth call-taker for those three months
answer_source: submission.md block 1 and generator/figures.json call.months_short, built 2026-10-16 (stage 3 of the stage 4 hardening)
stakeholder_role: the agency's operations manager, who brings the FY2028 late-shift staffing request to the agency's board

spine.file: acd_call_detail (the agency's ACD detail export, January 2025 to September 2026: the legacy CSV to the 13 May 2025 NG911 cutover, then the i3 JSON Lines log)
spine.entity: one 911 call presented to the agency's ACD queue, with the time it was presented, answered or abandoned, and the call-taker's release and ready times

world.geography: United States (Tavish County, a fictional county; its consolidated 911 agency and regional board are fictional)
world.org_type: a consolidated county emergency communications agency (primary public safety answering point)

driver: Units waiting for a service leave when the wait outlasts their own patience, so the queue each new unit meets is drained by those who give up; a model in which every unit waits until served overstates every wait; the patience that sets the drain is seen in full only for the units that left, the served ones showing only a lower bound, so it has to be estimated over every unit's wait, not from the leavers' waits; and the units arriving in the window being forecast give up far sooner than the history's average unit, so it has to be estimated on their own segment, where one pooled patience leaves the forecast as pessimistic as the standard queue.
driver_concrete: Tavish County's 911 callers on Friday and Saturday nights from 22:00 would hold on about two minutes, the rest of the week's about ten: the ACD log times every call's wait and marks the hang-ups, so the late shift's patience is the total time its 15,814 calls waited over the 81 that hung up (123.2 seconds), not the hang-ups' own mean wait (37.6 seconds) and not one patience over every call (576.6 seconds); Erlang A with that patience, the busy time from answer to ready (226.9 seconds) and the board's FY2028 hourly forecast puts only June, July and August below 90 per cent within 15 seconds with four call-takers, where Erlang C and one patience for every call put May to September below and the hang-ups' own waits leave no month short.
stump: A strong solver runs the standard Erlang C staffing model on the board's FY2028 late-shift forecast with the measured busy time and four call-takers, finds May to September below the 90 per cent answer standard (July 2027 83 per cent) and asks for a fifth call-taker for those five months; the step that lands it there is treating every caller as waiting until answered, when the late shift's own callers hang up after about two minutes and those who hang up shorten the wait for those who stay, so only June, July and August fall short (July 88 per cent); one patience for the whole week (577 seconds) puts May to September short again and the hang-ups' own waits (38 seconds) leave no month short.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who joins the legacy and NG911 ACD exports, reads the call-answering standard and the board's volume forecast correctly and runs Erlang C on each month's forecast late-shift hours with the measured busy time and four call-takers files five months below 90 per cent, May to September (July 2027 83 per cent), and a fifth call-taker for them; modelling the hang-ups with one patience estimated over every call in the history (576.6 seconds) files the same five months; the patience read off the hang-ups' own waits files no month short or July alone; carrying fiscal 2026's observed compliance forward (five call-takers) files none; only Erlang A with the late shift's own patience, estimated over every one of its calls' waits and censored where the call was answered, puts June, July and August below 90 and the rest above.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is each month's late-shift 911 answer-time compliance under the call-answering standard with the funded call-takers, which a PSAP staffing analysis computes from a queueing model of its own calls; because 911 callers hang up, and the late shift's far sooner than the week's, the model is Erlang A calibrated on the agency's ACD log with the late shift's own patience estimated over its censored waits; with another field's nouns there is no 15-second 911 answer standard, no call-taker busy time running to the CAD entry, no hang-up behaviour of 911 callers that changes with the night's call mix and no NG911 re-routing for the forecast to carry.
layer1: the ACD detail export in two layouts across the 13 May 2025 NG911 cutover: legacy CSV in local time to the second, then the i3 JSON Lines log in UTC with milliseconds, wireline calls on the legacy trunks to 16 May so both files carry those days with different calls
transferred-in calls from other PSAPs presented with their own arrival time, test calls answered by the i3 test responder, and redials after hang-ups in the same export
the late shift running across midnight and across daylight-saving changes, so a Friday shift ends on Saturday
the floor roster by block and night, a block past midnight dated by the evening it starts, late-shift sick calls noted as backfilled on overtime
the regional board's volume forecast as a long table for four PSAPs by month, day and hour beginning, a FY2027 sheet beside the FY2028 one
the i3 log carrying both ESInet identifiers, the backup centre's call-handling system filing location records under the incident identifier during planned works
one callback desk for 911 and administrative-line abandons, one open task per number, its log in local time without an offset

differentiation.task133: task133 prices a loan book's lifetime losses on loans watched only from an earlier platform's go-live (delayed entry); here nothing is a loan or a lifetime: the forecast is a 911 center's hourly answer-time compliance in a queue where callers hang up, and the decisive move is the queueing model with reneging and a patience estimated over waits the answer censors.
differentiation.task130: task130 prices a cover paying only for events first reported inside its own window (and, in a lineage architecture, regression to the mean); here the censoring is of each caller's patience by the answer, not of a report date, and it calibrates how a queue drains, not what events cost.
differentiation.task146: task146 sizes a pool of refused units released at a calendar turn, weighed by when each refusal fell; here no pool is released: each hour's compliance is set by how a queue drains when callers give up, a stationary queueing model per hour on the board's forecast arrivals.
differentiation.task142: task142 builds the upper percentile of a period's total from arrivals and how long each runs, with no waiting and no standard; here arrivals and busy times feed a waiting-time standard and the decisive quantity is the callers' abandonment, which shortens the others' waits.
differentiation.task149: task149's recordable rate per hour rises with work pace under an operating plan; here no rate is forecast: the hourly arrivals are the board's filed forecast and the decisive move is the queue's reneging and its censored calibration.
differentiation.task254: task254's architecture 2 estimates a time-to-event cut from events seen only before a lock date, each with its own truncation time; here nothing is truncated by a calendar date: each caller's patience is censored by the answer in a queue, and the patience feeds a queueing model with reneging whose drain on the queue decides each hour's compliance.
differentiation.task501: task501's architecture 2 strikes a forward figure from the pacing base that survives a walk-forward test; here no base is chosen by a back-test: the queueing model with reneging is forced by the callers' hang-ups in the ACD log, and its patience by the censoring of every answered call's wait.

lineage.fate: spent 2026-10-16 at stage 4: the determinism judge returned NOT_DETERMINISTIC, SEND_BACK (underspecified_objective): implementing the write-up's own method (standing-alone rates by six-month band, the group's first failure, 91.8 per cent charge-off share) filed $11.7 million against the golden $10 million (split 2.33, 3.59, 5.77 against 2.0, 3.0, 5.0), and the Section 1112 table and the net charge-offs did not reproduce (multi-instalment lines with no findable allocation rule; 'net' undefined; 38 ledger rows with no note number in the master); the rule 3 audit read AT_RISK (executing the loan authorization's cross-default clause on the register gives most of the move, the member hazard's double count at 1.19 the only analytical margin) and the shell (domain, task type, decision, role, register artifact, the default path's wording, a servicing conversion) as task133's
lineage.driver: A unit's failure takes down every other unit its backer carries, so the hazard each unit faces is the sum of the hazards of all the units behind the same backer, each at its own age, including units outside the population being priced and units added recently at the steepest part of the curve; a rate built on each unit alone at its own age, pooled over the history or taken from the latest period, prices every unit as if it stood alone.
lineage.driver_concrete: Many of the bank's borrowers are owner-operators who personally guarantee a 7(a) loan on each of several businesses under cross-default, so when one business fails the bank accelerates every loan the guarantor stands behind; each performing FY2019-21 loan's default hazard is the union of its guarantor group's business failure hazards at each business's own months on book, estimated on loans standing alone, the 1,561 businesses financed outside the pool included (1,403 of them in FY2026 and only now entering their peak years).
